title: Streaks and Slots — goal pivot notes (Ian Murphy)
content:
Quick context: trying a small personal experiment for the next 12 weeks to get more meaningful engineering output without burning out. Idea: combine 90-minute deep slots (3/day max) + a visible streak tracker + weekly micro-retrospectives. This doc is my running scratchpad: metrics, small KRs, blockers, and quick tactics.

Why now:
- Q4 felt noisy: lots of interrupts, shallow meetings, stalled mid-sized projects.
- I want 2 shipped infra improvements before the next planning cycle.
- Curious whether cadence + visible streaks nudges behavior more than rigid task lists.

Principles:
- Protect 3 x 90m deep slots on workdays (morning, post-lunch, late afternoon) — no meetings except critical.
- Measure weekly output as "meaningful merges" (PRs that touch infra or shipping signals) + time-in-deep-work hours.
- Small scoped KRs (30% time on project work, 70% maintenance/ops) — attempt to flip to 50/50 by week 10.

Personal OKR (12-week):
O: Ship two small infra improvements that reduce end-to-end batch latency and make my on-call life easier.
KR1: Merge and roll out batching config autodetect (INF-8423) to staging by week 6. (Target: reduce p95 token latency by 10% on synthetic workload)
KR2: Add an automated tracing alert + dashboard for the KV cache eviction path (PR #612) by week 8. (Target: reduce mean-time-to-detect from 18m to <6m)
KR3: Maintain a 14-day deep-work streak at least twice during the 12-week window.

Weekly check-in template (what I actually fill):
- Week: 2026-02-22 → 2026-02-28
- Deep-work hours: 11.5h (slots hit: 9/15)
- Merges: 2 meaningful (batch-config branch + small test refactor)
- Win: got batch-config prototype running on local AWS profile; saw median improvement in synthetic bench ~8%
- Fail/blocked: flaky system tests on staging; need better isolation for GPU-backed tests.
- Hypothesis to try: run GPU-backed tests in a separate ephemeral pool with a narrower image set — reduces test noise.
- Next week focus: unblock staging tests, finish the tracing PR skeleton, schedule a 30m sync with SRE.

Metrics I track (simple, not perfect):
- Deep slot success rate (slots hit / slots planned): weekly percentage as a single number.
- Meaningful merges (count): merges touching runtime/serving-runtime or console tooling.
- Time-to-detect incidents (minutes): rolling average across on-call incidents I own.
- Context switches per day: rough count (notifications that force me to drop slot).

Baseline (week 0):
- Deep slot success: 40%
- Meaningful merges / week: 0.6
- Time-to-detect incidents: 18m
- Context switches/day: 6-8

Experiment log (short):
- 2025-10-08: Started 90m blocks. Felt good for creative tasks but hard to protect after lunch slot.
- 2025-11-10: Added "meeting-free morning" rule; slots hit increased ~10 percentage points.
- 2026-01-12: Introduced a visual streak tracker in private Notion. Short-term motivator.
- 2026-02-14: Began pairing with Maya for 1 slot/week to move INF-8423 faster. Good for momentum.

Current blockers (actionable):
- Staging test noise: open ticket INF-8423 — need to scope test isolation plan; action: propose ephemeral GPU matrix by Fri.
- CI flakiness: follow up with Release Eng (ticket REL-119) — add test tagging and quarantine flaky tests.
- Calendar creep: need a short slack macro to mark calendar as DO NOT BOOK for slots.

Short TODOs (now-ish):
- Draft tracing dashboard layout and share with SRE by Mon (15m).
- Split the big staging test into two smaller suites; add env tagging (30m).
- Update PR #612 with simplified instrumentation and re-run bench (45m).
- Sync w/ Maya: Wed 11am (30m) to pair on autodetect config tuning.

Notes to self (raw):
- If a slot is interrupted, try to finish a "micro-commit" (10–15m) before switching — lowers restart friction.
- Use the Pomodoro-ish 50/10 inside 90m if attention sags.
- When frustrated, write a 3-line note in the doc: what blocked me + one small next step.

Questions / unresolved:
- Is the 90m length optimal for debugging kernel-level perf issues? Maybe shorter focused runs work better. Experiment with 60m during week 7.
- Should I try morning-only deep slots for two weeks to see if that consolidates flow?

Small wins log (motivation):
- 2026-02-03: Rewrote a flaky test and removed a shim — saved ~20m per CI run on average.
- 2026-02-18: Small perf config change improved median batch latency on local bench by 6%.

If I have to pivot (criteria):
- If deep-slot success < 30% for 4 consecutive weeks, re-evaluate format and cut to 2 slots/day or go to 50m slots.
- If meaningful merges / month < 1 for 6 weeks, reconsider scope/expectations and get feedback from manager.

References / useful links:
- Jira: INF-8423 (batching autodetect)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/612
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Batching+throughput+notes
- Slack thread: #eng-batching (search: "autodetect spikes")

Final quick-plan for next 7 days:
- Mon: propose ephemeral GPU test matrix; update INF-8423 with test plan (1h)
- Tue: small bench run + update PR #612 (1.5h)
- Wed: pair w/ Maya (1 slot) and carve afternoon slot for dashboard sketch (90m)
- Thu: triage CI flakes with Release Eng (30m)
- Fri: weekly micro-retro + update streak tracker + plan next week (20m)

---
Footnote: keep this doc lightweight and public-private: share with close collaborators (Maya, Ravi) but keep the streak tracker personal. If something is working, copy lessons to shared team notes (console-and-tooling or serving-runtime).
